posts.author: Suraj_Jha
posts.community: TruAlt Bioenergy - A bioenergy story or just a story?
posts.text: Earnings are in downtrend & p/e is inflated & it is incorrect metrics to use for praj. The numbers will compress significantly once the legacy business meets tailwinds again. Earnings have reduced not because they lost market share or they had a bad product , but because of over capacity. I am also not saying buy praj . I am saying praj might be a supirior company . They are trying to diversify into non govt dependent buisness which also gives them optionality.

posts.author: rshankv
posts.community: TruAlt Bioenergy - A bioenergy story or just a story?
posts.text: The question as per me is not “why not buy Praj”, but what does Praj has to offer? its revenue is on the downward trajectory, margins have shrunk and also profits have halved year on year and its trading at 125 PE, what is the growth of Praj vis a vis with TruAlt?

posts.author: novice2014
posts.community: TruAlt Bioenergy - A bioenergy story or just a story?
posts.text: As per the news reports, sugar production deficit is likely and Govt may ask sugar companies to reduce ethanol production. In this scenario, companies with grain based ethanol production should do well. CBG and SAF r other optionality, particularly in light of recent CBG incentive policy.

posts.author: Suraj_Jha
posts.community: TruAlt Bioenergy - A bioenergy story or just a story?
posts.text: The opportunity is real . The only issue I see with the whole space is that it depends totally on government policy. If we see policy tailwinds then a politically connected company should do better The reason I mentioned Praj , is that it does everything this company does . Is beaten down , cheap wrt historical valuations , but they are also trying to get into other business avenues which are not govt dependent. I personally think that the management is open about the headwinds & is competent

posts.community: TruAlt Bioenergy - A bioenergy story or just a story?
posts.text: almost all the ethanol and sugar players in India are politically linked as the sector itself is politically sensitive.

posts.author: Sriram_Palaniappan
posts.community: TruAlt Bioenergy - A bioenergy story or just a story?
posts.text: Yes, it is true if the company only produces ethanol and depends on OMCs offtake. However, if the company successfully commercializes its SAF business and expands its CBG business, a significant volume of ethanol could be used as a raw material for SAF production, while derivatives such as press mud and spent wash could be utilized for CBG production.

posts.author: vinay_turaidar
posts.community: TruAlt Bioenergy - A bioenergy story or just a story?
posts.text: The biggest problem is narrative against ethanol , which can crash the whole company.

posts.author: Sriram_Palaniappan
posts.community: TruAlt Bioenergy - A bioenergy story or just a story?
posts.text: TruAlt is the first company in this sector that I have covered indepth. I have not gone deep into Praj. I wanted to cover TruAlt as it has the potential to acheive higher profitability in future. I thought I could play CBG and SAF themes more directly than through an EPC company. But ofcource if the promoter’s political background is a concern, it would be better to stay away from this stock.

posts.author: Suraj_Jha
posts.community: TruAlt Bioenergy - A bioenergy story or just a story?
posts.text: Why choose this over praj? There is no question on the management quality or the engineering quality of praj . Similar market cap , cleaner management .
